nodes.speaker: ops
nodes.text: The 14-day lunar night is coming. No Sun, and -170°C outside. How do we prepare?

variants.text: The 14-day lunar night is coming. Our small ground panels will be useless in the dark. How do we prepare?
The 14-day lunar night is coming. Even the tall array can't catch sunlight that isn't there. How do we prepare?

nodes.fact: A lunar night lasts about 14 Earth days, and the surface can drop below -170°C.

nodes.speaker: eng
nodes.text: Alarm! A seal in the water recycler is failing. If it blows, we lose water.

variants.text: Alarm! A seal in the water recycler is failing, the same kind we never tested before launch.
Alarm! A seal in the water recycler is failing. After the rough launch, we're not surprised.

nodes.fact: The space station recycles about 90% of its water, including astronaut sweat and breath moisture.

nodes.speaker: arch
nodes.text: We have no spare seal. We could print one from moondust, or borrow one from the rover.
nodes.fact: Engineers are testing ways to melt lunar soil into bricks and parts with sunlight or lasers, a kind of moondust 3D printing.
